acceptance_signals: The dated development log records a complete pre-migration inventory of all current README second-level sections, their Product, Reference, Architecture, or Evidence responsibility, and their confirmed existing destination or retained product role.

README presents no more than three primary first-screen routes: Quickstart, one governed example, and architecture; the former Interview snapshot is a neutral product overview and reviewer-specific navigation remains available through existing reviewer documentation.

Stable 0.2.1, published prerelease 0.3.0rc1, and current development-source behavior are distinguished early, including the development-only doctor boundary, without implying publication or consumer adoption.
README retains exactly one overview architecture diagram and routes detailed architecture to existing architecture documents and ADRs.

Detailed commands, reference material, and chronological evidence are removed from the README reading path only after their existing owning documents are confirmed; no new catch-all reference is created and no unique claim is deleted.

Documentation tests enforce the new responsibility boundaries and continue protecting release identity, authority limits, link integrity, and unique evidence at its owning STATUS or dated-log surface rather than requiring historical evidence to be duplicated in README.
DEVELOPMENT_PLAN, STATUS, and the dated log accurately record the completed bounded slice, validation state, remaining reader-comprehension evidence, and next product review.
Focused documentation tests, the supported full test suite, task and repository governance checks, scope reconciliation, privacy scans, and git diff checks pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-888c9e3c6cb847919b6ac3e3fdec9841 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Inventory and classify every current README section as Product, Reference, Architecture, or Evidence, then refactor README into a concise reader-centered product entry that presents exactly three primary first-screen routes, distinguishes stable, published prerelease, and development-source behavior early, retains one overview architecture diagram, and routes detailed commands, architecture, reviewer material, and historical evidence to their existing owning documents without creating a new catch-all reference.

items: Compressing README could delete or obscure a unique release, authority, workflow, or evidence claim.
Changing tests that currently require historical claims in README could weaken coverage unless each claim remains asserted at its owning STATUS or dated-log surface.
Existing external links or repository anchors could break when headings and detailed sections are removed.
The compact entry could blur stable, prerelease, and development-source capabilities.
A responsibility inventory could accidentally become a new permanent catch-all reference rather than bounded migration evidence.
The user-owned untracked .codex directory and unrelated external consumer task remain outside this task.
Reviewed assumption: The latest strategic plan and current-status snapshot establish the selected README refactor direction and its acceptance boundaries.

Reviewed assumption: Existing topical documents provide confirmed destinations for detailed commands, architecture, onboarding, troubleshooting, consumer CI, release channels, governance contracts, and reviewer evidence.
Reviewed assumption: The dated development log is the correct owner for the one-time section classification and migration evidence.
Reviewed assumption: README may link to current STATUS and dated evidence without duplicating their chronological content.
Reviewed assumption: A concise product entry can preserve one shortest verified stable journey while routing advanced development-source workflows to their existing guides.
Reviewed unknown: Real two-to-three-minute comprehension by an unbriefed reader remains unproven until a later human review.
Reviewed unknown: Any section or claim found during full inventory without a confirmed owner or destination will trigger the declared stop condition and remain unmigrated.

title: Refactor README into a concise product entry
